title: Design System: Incursion Red River Item List

display.purpose: Hub headline only; clamped 36-64px, sentence case, tight -0.04em tracking, relaxed to -0.02em in Chinese.

headline.purpose: Selected build name on the bench; 26-38px, tightening to 28px below 640px.

title.purpose: Hub branch-card titles; 20-27px. Panel names stay at 12-13px and are not this step.

body.purpose: Prose and guidance in the system sans at 14px/1.5, with narrower measures for supporting copy.

control.purpose: Button, nav, and copy-bar labels at 12px/600 sans; rail names sit one step up at 13px/600.

label.purpose: Field and section labels: 11px mono uppercase with 0.08-0.16em tracking.

measure.purpose: The amber stat pair only: 44px/600 mono, tabular numerals, -0.035em tracking.

data.purpose: Command preview and long machine strings: 11.5px/1.55 mono.

shadows.name: active-underline
shadows.purpose: Pressed top-nav links and segmented-control options; separates current from hovered.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Search field focus, paired with a cyan border.

shadows.name: toast-lift
shadows.purpose: The transient copy-confirmation toast; the only cast shadow in the product.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: Trace draw, node entrance, drawer slide, and the hub schematic draw.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Color, border, background, and opacity state changes.

motion.name: trace-draw
motion.purpose: Schematic branch trace drawing, staggered 22ms per node.

motion.name: node-in
motion.purpose: Slot and kit node entrance, staggered 16ms, delayed 380ms after its trace.

narrative.overview:
The site is an instrument on a dark workbench, not a game UI. Its primary surface is a three-lane bench: a weapon rail on the left, a dot-grid stage in the center where a line-drawn weapon sits inside a tree of hairline traces, and a readout lane on the right that ends in the command the player copies. The hub is the same instrument seen from the door: one display headline, one line schematic, and two branch cards into the bench and the terminal. Everything is near-black, green-tinted, and dense, but the density is ordered — rail, stage, readout — so the loadout can be read before a single line of the command.

The palette assigns jobs instead of decorating. Phosphor green is the machine (structure, selection, action); cyan is every identifier the player must trust or copy exactly; amber is every measurement. Names and prose are set in the OS's own sans because the site may never fetch a font; every ID, field label, and number is monospace. The result is a dual voice — human names, machine data — that stays legible in two languages without translating a single item ID.

The world's refusals are confirmed by both the direction contract and the build: no glass or backdrop blur, no outer glow, no gradient text, no game renders or icon illustrations standing in for the schematic. Depth is tonal and linear, never cast. The loudest element on the bench is the measurement readout; the only large green fill is the copy button. Those two signals never multiply: one reading and one copy action per view.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black green-tinted ground (#030504), one panel step lighter (#050a07), hairline structure
Green system signal, cyan identifiers, amber measurements — no fourth accent
System sans for names and prose; monospace for every ID, label, and measurement
Three-lane bench on desktop, stacked bench plus fixed copy bar on narrow screens
Dot-grid schematic stage with 1px curved branch traces and compact slot nodes
Compact corners (3–12px), flat-by-default surfaces, a single 58px topbar offset

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: Green is the system and the action, cyan is an identifier, amber is a measurement. No screen adds a fourth accent hue, and no value swaps channels: a stat never turns green, an ID never turns amber, a selected border never turns cyan.

rules.name: The Near-Black Ground Rule
rules.body: Ground and panel stay within one step of each other (#030504 to #050a07), and tinted washes never exceed 11% alpha. A full green surface fill is reserved for the primary copy button, the skip link, and text selection; everything else signals with 1px lines and washes.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Anything copied, typed, measured, or identified is monospace with tabular numerals; names and prose are sans. Setting a weapon name in mono is a category error, and setting an item ID in sans is an offence against copyability.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-A-Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase plus 0.08–0.16em tracking belongs to 11px mono field and section labels only. Display headlines and weapon names stay sentence case, in both languages.

rules.name: The Bilingual Tracking Rule
rules.body: Switching to Chinese relaxes display tracking (-0.04em to -0.02em), opens its line-height (0.98 to 1.08), and shrinks its clamp; mono labels keep Latin tracking. Section names and UI strings translate — weapon names and item IDs never do.

rules.name: The Three-Lane Rule
rules.body: A wide bench has exactly rail, stage, readout. The center lane is reserved for the schematic — no data table, no second list, no marketing block displaces the weapon.

rules.name: The One-Click-Away Rule
rules.body: The full command is always rendered or fixed on screen: last block of the readout on desktop, a fixed copy bar on narrow screens. Never bury the copy action behind a tab or an overflow menu.

rules.name: The 58px Constant Rule
rules.body: The topbar is 58px tall and every sticky offset derives from it. A new sticky surface uses the same constant rather than inventing a second header height.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, rails, readouts, and the stage are flat at rest. If a new surface needs to separate, lift the tone by one step or draw a hairline — do not add a drop shadow.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Selection and focus are a 1px border, a wash of 11% or less, and a 2px cyan outline. Outer glows, halo shadows, and backdrop blur are refused.

rules.name: The Compact-Corner Rule
rules.body: Controls stop at 7–8px, the stage at 10px, hub cards at 12px. Pills belong to scrollbar thumbs and nothing else; no rounded-full buttons, inputs, or tags.

rules.name: The 1px Structure Rule
rules.body: Every structural edge starts as a 1px hairline at 16% green. Interactive borders start at 30% and may escalate to full green on hover or selection; panels are never framed at 2px. The only 2px rules are the active-tab underline and the focus outline.

rules.name: The Selection-Is-A-Wash Rule
rules.body: Selected and current states are a 1px green border plus an 11% green wash, and on horizontal tabs a 2px inset underline. Text does not invert to green-on-black except on the primary button and skip link; the selection marker is a 4px square, not a background fill.

rules.name: The Diagram-Disclaimer Rule
rules.body: Any schematic carries the SCHEMATIC · NOT A GAME RENDER caption and the bench-foot sentence that grouping is inferred and in-game success is unverified. A schematic without both is off-system.

dos: Do draw structure with the hairline tokens (rgba(126,226,162,0.16) for dividers, 0.3 for interactive borders) before reaching for a fill or shadow.
Do keep measurements amber and tabular (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; the pair is 44px/600 mono), and keep identifiers cyan in mono at 11px.
Do keep every copied ID character-exact — casing, underscores, and game-side spellings intact — and never translate weapon names or IDs.
Do show state with more than color: the rail adds a 4px dot, tabs add an inset 2px underline, inputs add a 1px ring.
Do keep the global focus treatment: 2px cyan outline, 2px offset, 4px radius.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: the trace draw, node entrance, drawer, toast, and hero draw all resolve instantly.
Do keep prose measures tight — 34ch for the stat note, 44ch for card copy, 56ch for hub intro, 62ch for the bench foot, 78ch for the hub footer.
Do use the primary green button once per view: copy full build in the readout, or copy command in the mobile bar.
Do keep the OS font stacks; the site must work offline with no external font request.
donts: Don't add glass, backdrop blur, outer glow, or gradient text. Existing gradients are functional — sticky group-title fades, the dot-grid mask, the stage vignette — never decoration or text fills.
Don't put game screenshots, weapon renders, or illustrated icons on the bench; the only weapon imagery is the authored line schematic.
Don't invent a label or unit for the stat pair, or a compatibility claim for a slot; show the source reading and the unverified note.
Don't use green for a stat value, amber for an identifier, or cyan for an action; the three signal channels do not swap.
Don't introduce a light theme, a second surface family, or a saturated panel fill.
Don't set weapon or build names in uppercase or in mono, and don't add letterspacing to display headlines.
Don't use pill radii on buttons, inputs, or tags; 99px is for scrollbar thumbs only.
Don't replace the 1px hairline with a 2px frame or a cast shadow to create hierarchy; use the one-step tonal lift instead.
